objective: Application, cryptographic, and password attacks and their indicators: injection, buffer overflow, replay, privilege escalation, forgery, directory traversal; downgrade, collision, and birthday attacks; password spraying and brute force; indicators such as account lockout, concurrent session usage, blocked content, impossible travel, resource consumption, resource inaccessibility, out-of-cycle logging, published/documented compromise, and missing logs
secondaryObjectives: Data sources for an investigation: log data (firewall logs, application logs, endpoint logs, OS-specific security logs, IPS/IDS logs, network logs, metadata) and other data sources (vulnerability scans, automated reports, dashboards, packet captures)

Incident response activities as SY0-701 names them: preparation, detection, analysis, containment, eradication, recovery, lessons learned; training; testing (tabletop exercise, simulation); root cause analysis; threat hunting; digital forensics (legal hold, chain of custody, acquisition, reporting, preservation, e-discovery)

brief.situation: You are the analyst on shift in the security operations center (SOC) at Larkspur Supply, a fictional distributor with 200 staff. At 09:00 the SIEM raises an impossible-travel alert on jpike, an accounts payable clerk, and two coworkers have reported an 'Invoice overdue' email. Work the incident: investigate, contain, preserve evidence, and report.
handover: Mail and sign-in logs, the mail gateway, the web proxy and the directory are all in the console. Audit logs are kept for 90 days.
The incident response plan says: contain confirmed account takeovers at once, preserve evidence before purging or wiping, escalate to the incident lead.
howItWorks: Each task takes analyst time: choose it, then let the work finish, which moves the clock by the minutes that task takes. The attacker keeps working on the same clock.
New alerts and log lines appear in the console as they happen. Pick an account, an indicator or a host in each action's options.
When you declare the incident contained, you notify, write the record and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the incident record: what showed this was an account takeover, why you contained it the way you did, and what evidence you kept and why.

parts.label: Indicators
parts.criteria: Names the indicators: impossible travel (two sign-ins 20 minutes apart from Tacoma and an overseas hosting provider), an MFA push the user did not start, and the reported phishing email with a credential page; links them to SY0-701 2.4 indicators.
parts.modelAnswer: Two successful sign-ins 20 minutes apart from Tacoma and a hosting provider overseas is impossible travel; the second came with an MFA push jpike approved without starting a sign-in, and he had opened a credential page from the reported invoice email. Together they show stolen credentials used by someone else.

parts.label: Containment choice
parts.criteria: Explains why disabling the account and revoking sessions comes before a password reset alone (a reset leaves the attacker's session signed in), and why persistence (inbox rules, added MFA methods) and other recipients must be checked before closing.
parts.modelAnswer: A reset alone leaves the stolen session working, so I disabled the account and revoked every session first. Then I checked the mailbox for forwarding rules and added sign-in methods, searched every mailbox for the message, blocked the domain and purged it, so the attacker had no way back in.

parts.label: Evidence
parts.criteria: Says what was preserved (sign-in and mailbox audit logs, the message with headers, a triage collection from the laptop), that it was done before purging or wiping, and that handling was recorded (chain of custody).
parts.modelAnswer: Before purging or wiping anything I exported the sign-in and mailbox audit logs, saved the message with full headers, took a triage collection from the laptop, and recorded hashes and who handled each item, so the chain of custody holds.

reasoningCriteria.label: Written indicators, containment choice and evidence

expertPath.text: Read the sign-in log: impossible travel and an approved push mean takeover. Disable jpike and revoke sessions; escalate.
Search every mailbox for the message and block the domain and URL before anyone else clicks.
Preserve the logs, the message with headers and a laptop triage collection; then purge the message.
Check jpike's rules, forwarding and sign-in methods; close and notify the incident lead, management, legal and finance.

contained.headline: Good: contained, scoped and preserved
contained.body: You shut the session before the attacker could build persistence or spread, checked who else was exposed, and kept the evidence before cleaning up.

containedLate.headline: Contained, with gaps
containedLate.body: The attacker is out. The criteria show what came late: containment past 30 minutes, a second account, or evidence purged before it was kept.

fraud.headline: Payment fraud
fraud.body: A password reset alone, or no containment, left the attacker's session in the mailbox. Disable the account and revoke sessions first; a reset does not end a stolen session.

evidenceLost.headline: Evidence wiped
evidenceLost.body: Reimaging before collecting removes the only proof of what ran on the laptop. Preserve first (RS.AN-07), then recover.

stillIn.headline: Closed too soon
stillIn.body: An open session, a second compromised account or an attacker's forwarding rule or authenticator is a way back in. Account for every means of persistent access before eradication (CISA).

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: No record was written before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: Impossible travel plus an MFA push the user did not start is account takeover. Disable the account and revoke its sessions at once (a reset leaves the session alive), escalate, find every recipient and block the domain and URL, preserve logs, the message and a laptop collection before purging or wiping, remove the attacker's inbox rule and authenticator, then notify the incident lead, management, legal and finance and record the root cause and scope.
